newsitem.title: USA: Continental earnings fall; AMR profits up 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: Continental earnings fall; AMR profits up 23 pct.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. Wednesday reported sharply lower profits for the third quarter, blaming the downturn on the cost of updating its fleet of planes.
AMR Corp., the parent of American Airlines, the nation's second largest carrier, said its earnings increased 23 percent but it also complained that its costs were still too high.
Continental said it earned $18 million, or 25 cents a share, in the latest quarter, down from year-ago earnings of $111 million, or $1.34 a share. Revenues rose to $1.76 billion from $1.5 billion.
Continental said excluding special expenses, it had operating income of $101 million, or $1.28 a share, which the company said was in line with Wall Street's expectations.
The airline said it took a charge of $77 million in the third quarter to cover the cost of replacing old aircraft with new planes and a $6 million charge for early debt retirement.
The company said it prepaid $324 million of debt, which should save $6 million in annual interest payments in the first year.

Continental Chief Executive Gorden Bethune said in a conference call with reporters that the company's "booking trends look very good" and it was "expecting a very good fourth quarter." He declined to be more specific.
Continental officials also said the airline has hedged itself against a jump in fuel prices through mid-February. Rising fuel costs boosted the carrier's operating costs in the third quarter.

Separately, Bethune said Continental should reach a formal agreement with Air France in the next two weeks on a code sharing pact, which will coordinate ticket booking and feed their passengers back and forth.
Earlier, the company said it signed a letter of intent on a code sharing agreement with Air France. Delta is also linked with Air France.

Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR Corp. said its third quarter earnings rose to $282 million or $3.06 a share compared with year-ago earnings of $229 million or $2.96 a share. Revenues were also higher at $4.56 billion against $4.44 billion in the third quarter of 1995.
In a statement, AMR said it had a good third quarter though costs are still too high.
"Although our airline costs are still higher than we'd like them to be, we had a good third quarter," it said.
"Robust demand, a favourable pricing environment and the continued profitable growth of our non-airline businesses offset a dramatic increase in fuel prices," it said.
Continental's class A shares rose 62.5 cents at $24.75 while AMR was off $1.25 at $81.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
